stages.title: Competitive tendering: pros and cons
stages.sub: After this the student can weigh up the advantages and disadvantages of competitive tendering for public services.

steps.q: Three cleaning firms all want a council contract, so each one submits a price it would charge to do the work. Does the council now have one price to consider, or several to compare?
steps.hint: How many firms are trying to win the same job?

steps.right: Push it down to beat rivals
steps.wrong: Push it up to cover costs
steps.hint: If a higher price loses you the contract, what do you do to your price?

steps.q: A firm wins the contract by submitting a price barely covering its costs. Once the contract starts, is there much spare money left to pay staff well or use good materials?
steps.hint: If the price was pushed right down to win, what is left over once the job starts?

steps.q: With almost no spare money in the contract, what might the firm do to still turn a profit?
steps.right: Cut staff wages or corners on quality
steps.wrong: Raise staff wages and improve quality
steps.hint: If money is tight, where can the firm claw back profit?

steps.q: Only three huge firms are large enough to bid for a motorway contract, unlike the many small cleaning firms bidding for the council job earlier. Is it easier or harder for just these three to talk to each other and agree on prices than it was for many small rivals?
steps.right: Easier, there are so few of them
steps.wrong: Harder, there are so few of them
steps.hint: Think about how many firms would need to coordinate in each case.

steps.q: If those three firms secretly agree in advance who will win and at what price, does any real price rivalry still happen between their bids?
steps.right: No, the bidding is no longer genuine
steps.wrong: Yes, the bidding is still genuine
steps.hint: If the outcome is already agreed, what is left of the competition?

steps.q: A private waste firm has years of experience running efficient collection routes that the council itself has never had to develop. By tendering the contract out, can the council make use of this know-how?
steps.right: Yes, it can draw on that know-how
steps.wrong: No, it cannot draw on that know-how
steps.hint: Think about who actually holds the specialist skills here.
